evidence: /lists and /bookmarks are both registered in src/App.tsx; flows/screens.spec.ts opens both as customer1 with no page error.
useCommerceSlice exposes deleteList and removeFromList, and Lists.tsx uses both.
businessService.byIds / providerService.byIds fetch saved shops and providers with one .in("id", ids) query each; Bookmarks.tsx used to fire one request per saved row.
ProviderDetail has an 'Add to a list' action opening AddToListSheet (type PROVIDER) next to the heart, matching BusinessDetail.

createList inserts first and uses the id the database returns; the comment in useCommerceSlice records why (a temporary id makes the item insert fail its foreign key and the items are lost on refresh).

Confirmed still true: lists are private (RLS scopes them to their owner) and there is no public list route, so a curated list can't be shared. Sharing means a visibility column, a public route and a share sheet — a v1.1 feature, owner decision.
Emoji choices in AddToListSheet have aria-label, aria-pressed and a 44x44 minimum touch target.
CommunityPostDetail has the Recommend action (setRecommendOpen) and resolves recommendations through src/lib/communityRecommendations.ts.
The comment composer attaches a listing (post_comments.listing_type/listing_id, commentListing state in CommunityPostDetail).
Author actions exist: edit (EditPostSheet, opened from the feed card via router state), delete (deleteConfirm), mark resolved (resolvedBusy) and comment policy inside the edit sheet.

Comments have delete (own, or anyone's under your own post, plus the community_comment_delete permission), report (reportingComment) and pin, per the permissions comment at CommunityPostDetail ~line 445.
Bookmarks has a POST tab backed by communityService.savedPosts().
EditPostSheet edits media, alt text, per-type fields (lastSeen, reward, pickupNote), tagged listing, comment policy and hideLikeCount (20260930).

PublicProfile post cards navigate to /community/:id, and 'Hide from profile' is persisted (community_posts.show_on_profile, read back in userService.publicProfile and filtered for everyone but the owner).
CommunityHub has keyword search (20260931) feeding in_query of community_posts_feed.
CommunityCompose has an identity picker (identityPickerOpen) over the router-state seller context, and blocks posting until the identity settles.
CommunityCompose uses LocationPickerSheet; a pinned place wins over the author's GPS and the shop's address.
Poll votes can be cleared (communityService.clearVote) and the author can close a poll early (closePollNow → communityService.closePoll).
CommunityPostDetail opens PhotoViewer for the cover image and every gallery photo (cursor zoom-in, startIndex).

trg_notify_post_comment → notify_on_post_comment and trg_notify_comment_mention exist on post_comments (production, 2026-09-16); 20260974 fixed the story-reaction and recommendation notifiers in the same family.
cron.job on production: 'notify-ended-polls' runs select public.notify_ended_polls() every 10 minutes.
likes_count and comments_count are maintained by trg_sync_post_likes_count / trg_sync_post_comments_count (20260922); the client only reads them.
Recommendations go through the community_post_add_recommendation RPC instead of a read-modify-write on the array (which RLS also blocked).

The SELECT policy on community_posts is (NOT is_blocked_between(author_user_id)) and community_posts_feed is a STABLE sql function, so RLS applies to the caller: verified on staging that a blocked neighbour's post is visible before the block and gone after, while its author still sees it.
CommunityHub subscribes to UPDATE and DELETE on community_posts (separately from the insert counter) and refetches, so a deleted or resolved post stops sitting there stale.
trg_notify_comment_reaction → notify_on_comment_reaction exists on comment_reactions (production, 2026-09-16).
admin_delete_comment (admin-only, clears replies and reactions) plus report targets of type COMMENT in the admin queue; 20260982 adds the author notice and the audit row.
public.ratings carries trg_recompute_ratings and ratings_update_avg (production triggers, 2026-09-16), so rating_avg / rating_count follow every review.
public.ratings has an UPDATE policy (upd_ratings) alongside ins_ratings and read_ratings, so editing your own review persists.

RateScreen computes isRequester from the agreement and rates the other side, and requestService.rate takes an explicit ratee {type,id} so the provider or shop entity is rated, not the person (E2E-027). E2E critical/request-proposal-agreement covers it.
MyAppointments shows a 'Rate & Review' action on completed bookings (reviewingApt).
notify_on_rating handles BUSINESS (owner_user_id), PROVIDER (user_id) and USER ratees, each with its own deep link (production definition, 2026-09-16).
providerService.reviews selects owner_reply and maps ownerReply; ProviderDetail and BusinessDetail both render the owner's reply under the review.

businessService.addReview now busts the cached business row on both the insert and the update path (providerService.addReview already did), so the reviewer returns to the updated rating instead of the cached one.

ReviewSheet takes initialRating/initialComment and the detail screens pass businessService.myReview / providerService.myReview, so re-reviewing opens on what was written last time ('Edit your review') instead of blanking it.
Star buttons in ReviewSheet and RateScreen have aria-label, aria-pressed and a 44x44 minimum touch target.
BusinessSettings links to /business/:id/manage/reviews, and the review notification (notify_on_rating) deep-links straight there.
ReviewsManager renders ManageNav for businesses and ProviderManageNav for providers.
/provider/:id/manage/reviews is registered and served by the same ReviewsManager; reply_to_rating supports provider replies.
A posted reply can be edited: the card offers an edit action that refills the composer and the toast distinguishes 'Reply updated' from 'Reply posted'.
Both review routes sit inside the console guards, and the business one inside RequireOwner, so an unprivileged visitor is bounced before the screen renders rather than failing on submit.
ReviewsManager renders 'No reviews yet' and, with a star filter on, 'No reviews with N stars'.

reply_to_rating accepts a delegate with the business 'leads' scope (20260974, verified on staging), so the database no longer blocks them. The screen itself is deliberately owner-only (RequireOwner in App.tsx, 'FULL delegates and scoped team members are bounced') — opening it to delegates is a one-line route change if that product call ever changes.
With a star filter on, the header reads 'N of M reviews' instead of the unfiltered total.
ProviderDetail builds displayVouches by checking whether the viewer is already in the list (isUserInVouchList) before adding or removing their own bubble, so nobody is counted or drawn twice.
userService.publicProfile counts vouches received — vouches.provider_id in the user's own provider ids — not vouches given, so 'Well Vouched' can't be earned by vouching for others.
socialService.addVouch, removeVouch and the endorsement methods all throw on { error } instead of discarding it, so a rejected write surfaces rather than leaving optimistic state wrong.

trg_prevent_self_vouch on vouches and trg_prevent_self_endorsement on endorsements both run check_self_vouch (production, 2026-09-16). Verified on staging as the provider's own account: both inserts fail with CANNOT_VOUCH_FOR_SELF while a neighbour's succeed.
socialService.vouchCount does an exact head count for the headline number; the avatar list stays capped (now 50). The counter no longer stops at 20.
ProviderDetail merges the provider's declared skills into the endorsement list at count 0, so a newly added skill can receive its first endorsement instead of never appearing.

Confirmed absent by design for v1: vouches, endorsements and ratings are shown as separate signals, with badges derived from thresholds (PROFILE_BADGE_THRESHOLDS). A single composite trust score is a product decision — it changes what neighbours see about each other and needs a defined algorithm before it ships.
